projects.title: Portable Ventilator Re-design
projects.description:
For my senior design project, I worked with nine other students on a re-design of a portable emergency ventilator (PEV). The original model for the ventilator received FDA approval in the late 1980s, but it never reached the market. My group's goal was to create a final product targeted for the EMT market. Since we we had such a large group of people, we elected to split into two groups to start the project. I was the manager of the technical group, where we focused on the selection and testing of the mechanical and electrical parts. I was responsible for ensuring that we were completing tasks according to schedule and relaying any problems to the project manager. 

My personal contributions to this project were the selection and testing of a mass flow sensor, pressure sensor, and air compressor. To select these devices I performed an analysis based on fluid dynamics and then selected the final products based on our specifications (determined from the customer needs and the fluid analysis) and cost.

To test these parts, I worked with several different members of the group as I encountered unexpected problems with the hardware. While the testing of the pressure sensor was simple with the use of a barometer, the mass flow sensor and air compressor were much more difficult to test. Due to the pulsatile nature of the compressor, the mass flow sensor could not get an accurate reading. After discussing this with other group members and our customer, we determined that we needed a chamber to diffuse the flow before the mass flow sensor. I was able to determine the necessary volume for this chamber through testing, and, working with other members of the group, we developed designs using PVC tubing and 3D printing. Since neither of these would fit in the final housing layout, we eventually elected to seal off a compartment around the handle of the casing, which worked for our project but would not be ideal in a final product.

patents.title: BEAM DETECTION AND FILTERING NOISE
patents.description: A digital radiographic detector outputs positive read out signals that may oscillate. The presence of negative going portions of the read out signals may be used to determine that the detected positive signals are a result of noise, while an absence of the negative going portions may be used to determine that x- rays are impacting the detector.

patents.title: HIGH FRAME CAPTURE RATE SYNCHRONIZATION WITH STREAMING MODE
patents.description: A digital radiographic detector detects a first mode signal and dispositions a received digital image according to a procedure associated with the first mode signal. A second mode signal results in dispositioning a second received digital image according to a second image disposition procedure. The detector determines the first mode or second mode based on the signal's pulse width, a number and timing of rising edges (peaks), a digital code, a voltage level, or a combination thereof.
